profile.name: Faraz Khan
profile.title: Software Engineer · Backend
profile.tagline: I build reliable, secure backend systems — currently for a national online examination platform at TCS iON.
about: I'm a backend engineer with 3+ years at TCS iON, working on the online examination platform that runs exams nationally. I work mostly in Java and Spring Boot across microservices: content ingestion, search, and the security work around HTTPS and identity verification.

Because the exam systems run on TCS iON's own Linux build, a good part of my work is with the OS team. I make the application behave on locked-down exam machines and trace failures through system logs. Before TCS I freelanced as a full-stack developer, building Django apps and deploying them on AWS and Heroku.
Outside of work you'll find me on the football pitch. I played for my college team.

highlights: Played for the college football team
Built a college management system for SJCIT: attendance, marks and study materials

experience.description: Backend engineer on TCS iON's online examination platform, a microservices system that delivers high-stakes exams nationally on exam machines running TCS iON's own Linux build.
highlights: Cut search API retrieval time by ~35% over large exam datasets by tuning indexes, trimming query projections, removing N+1 queries and adding pagination
Implemented streaming HTTP multipart handling for mock-exam content bundles, with per-part validation and all-or-nothing processing
Migrated application traffic from HTTP to HTTPS with a fallback path, with no interruption to live examinations
Built Aadhaar-based identity verification with a cross-functional team, confirming candidate identity before and after each exam
Built a browser upgrader that detects, downloads and silently installs the required browser across the exam machines
Removed a startup dependency on another team's service by loading application context objects dynamically from the database
Worked with the OS team on the in-house Linux build and diagnosed field failures from application and system logs
Implemented watermarking and secure content display, refactored the React scientific calculator to support complex numbers, and delivered 15+ change requests

experience.description: Freelance full-stack work, owning each delivery end to end: requirements, build, deployment and client communication.
highlights: Built Django web applications with REST APIs
Wrote Python web-scraping scripts for data collection
Worked with MySQL and MongoDB, and deployed apps on AWS and Heroku

projects.title: Snapverse — Social Media Platform
projects.description: An Instagram-style social network. Users can sign up, share photo posts, like and save posts without page reloads (AJAX), comment, follow and unfollow each other, and chat in a built-in messenger. Each user has a profile page. An extended version screens chat messages for abusive and hate speech and suspends offending accounts.

projects.title: CampusHub — College Management System
projects.description: A college management portal built for SJCIT. Students and teachers have separate roles (teacher sign-up requires a verification password), and users can register with email, Google or Facebook. Teachers take attendance and enter exam marks; students see their marks and attendance, and study materials are organised by branch and semester.

projects.title: RescueIndia — COVID-19 Relief Platform
projects.description: Built during India's second COVID-19 wave (2021) to connect people who needed help with people who could give it. Patients request telemedicine consultations by sharing vitals like oxygen saturation and pulse. Doctors, counsellors, volunteers and donors register to help. It also has a hospital oxygen-shortage tracker, a directory of health-care providers, a community message board, and online donations through Stripe.
